title: How to normalize data to a 0-1 scale
task: Min-max scaling — put different-ranged metrics on one comparable footing.

excel.note: Anchor the range and fill down. The minimum maps to 0, the maximum to 1.

explanation: Subtracting the minimum shifts the scale to start at zero; dividing by the range squeezes it to end at one: 30 sits exactly halfway between 10 and 50 → 0.5. Useful before averaging unlike metrics (a 0-100 score with a 0-5 rating) or for progress bars. Two caveats: a constant column gives 0/0 (guard with IF(MAX=MIN,...)), and new data outside the original min/max lands outside 0-1 — recompute or clamp. For outlier-heavy data, the z-score recipe is the sturdier scaling.
